We had an excellent experience at Eye Care for Animals with my senior dog, Luke. From the moment we arrived, everyone was kind, professional, and incredibly organized. We were taken back right on time, which I really appreciated.

Luke can be a little fussy during veterinary appointments, but the staff handled him so well. They were able to complete all of his testing without any issues, and I never heard him getting upset while he was in the back, which tells me they really know how to work with animals.

Throughout the appointment, several members of the team came in to explain what they were finding and keep me updated on Luke's condition. They took the time to answer every one of my questions, explained everything thoroughly, and never made me feel rushed. I left with a much better understanding of what was going on and what our options were.

They were also very accommodating when it came time to pay, allowing me to split the bill between two credit cards without any hassle.

If your pet has a complicated eye issue, I highly recommend Eye Care for Animals. Their knowledge, professionalism, compassion, and excellent communication gave me complete confidence that Luke was in the best possible hands.

I brought my dog, Tyson, in to have his eyes checked after his recent diagnosis for blastomycosis.  I’ve learned that this systemic fungal disease can affect dogs’ eyes and vision very quickly and often without warning and I wanted to stay ahead of any issues Tyson could have with his eyes.  Everyone we encountered here was warm and caring and great with Tyson. Mario was the vet asst who did a few preliminary tests with Tyson and then Dr. Gaerig and her fellowship intern Dr. Laeti joined to perform more specific tests and discuss my concerns and Tyson’s results. I was very relieved to learn that Tyson showed no signs of blastomycosis damage or imminent damage to his eyes (all clear!).  It was also wonderful to discover that Dr. Gaerig is very knowledgeable about blastomycosis (not all vets are) which added to my relief.  I am thankful to have Dr. Gaerig and Eye Care for Animals available for Tyson’s care.

I’m sharing my experience as a long-term client. I brought my dog here for approximately three years, starting when he was about six months old. From early on, it was known that he had a congenital eye condition affecting both eyes.
At his initial visit, when he was about six months old, I was told that he would develop glaucoma and that eye removal would eventually be necessary. I brought him in every three to four months for eye pressure checks and was prescribed multiple prescription eye drops, which were adjusted and increased over time. I was consistently told that his pressures were elevating. At later visits, glaucoma was discussed as an established diagnosis.
Eventually, I was told that one eye’s pressure was too high and that it would need to be removed. I was also advised to remove the other eye at the same time, even though that eye was still in a normal pressure range and both eyes were still functional. Cost efficiency related to anesthesia was mentioned, and I was told that dogs generally adapt well to blindness and that owners tend to be more upset than the animals themselves.
As a pet owner, the thought of removing one eye was already extremely difficult. Being advised to remove both eyes and permanently blind my dog, despite the fact that he was not showing signs of pain, could see well, and his eyes appeared fine to me, did not feel right.
I chose to seek a second opinion from another veterinary ophthalmologist, who told me clearly that my dog does not have glaucoma. He explained that my dog’s elevated eye pressure is consistent with his congenital eye condition, that he was not even in pain, and that his eyes otherwise appeared stable.
It has now been nearly a year since that consultation. Since that time, my dog has not been on glaucoma medication and has not needed eye removal. His eyes no longer appear irritated, he scratches them far less than he did when he was on the eye drops, and he seems noticeably more comfortable overall. His vision has remained intact, and he is able to catch balls in the air, which he was not able to do before.
I’m grateful that I sought another opinion before making a permanent decision. Despite my dog’s known medical history and the fact that he was not in pain and could still see perfectly fine, irreversible recommendations were still made. Based on my experience, I would advise pet owners to seek a second opinion or consider avoiding this practice altogether when facing serious or irreversible recommendations

was recently referred to your hospital by my veterinarian for my dog’s eye condition. I contacted your office and was informed that the next available appointment would not be until November. I was also told that an emergency appointment could be scheduled sooner if I paid $1,000 upfront.

While I understand that specialty veterinary care is in high demand and that emergency appointments require additional resources, I found the way this information was communicated to be discouraging and concerning. The situation made me feel that access to urgent care for my pet was dependent more on payment than on medical need.

As a pet owner who is trying to do what is best for my dog, I believe that policies like this should be explained with more compassion and transparency. Clearer communication about what the emergency deposit covers and why it is required would help clients feel more supported during what is already a stressful time.
